/-!
# Preservation by `endUse` (O12, §69) and `free` (O13, §70)

Both effects only make authorities inactive and mark places dead, then release the authorities
whose holder died (§69, §70 `ok` effects). The shared argument is in namespace `EndFree`; the
per-operation results state that each step preserves `KInv` (§57) and `KAux` (§40, §49.7), and
the effects of §69 and §70: the ended place stays usable, its leaves become `Uninit`, transitively
owned storage and the released unit are dead, pinned leaves block the step (§69.4, §70.4).
-/

namespace Ern.MemoryModel.Access

namespace EndFree

/-! ## Authorities that are only released (§69, §70) -/

/-- The authorities of `s₁` are those of `s`, some of them made inactive (§69, §70 `ok` effects:
authorities are released, never created or changed otherwise). -/
def OnlyReleases (s s₁ : S3) : Prop :=
  s₁.A.length = s.A.length ∧ ∀ (j : Nat) (z : Authority), s₁.A[j]? = some z →
    ∃ y, s.A[j]? = some y ∧ z.mode = y.mode ∧ z.origin = y.origin ∧ z.footprint = y.footprint ∧
      z.holder = y.holder ∧ (z.active = true → y.active = true)

/-- Mapping the authorities by a function that keeps an authority or makes it inactive only
releases authorities (§69, §70). -/
theorem map_releases {s s₁ : S3} {g : Authority → Authority} (hA : s₁.A = s.A.map g)
    (hg : ∀ y, g y = y ∨ g y = { y with active := false }) : OnlyReleases s s₁ := by
  refine ⟨by rw [hA, List.length_map], fun j z hz => ?_⟩
    · simp at hx
    · exact hx
  obtain ⟨y, hy, ya⟩ := h3 q hq₀ x hx₀
  have hc := hpre.anchors q (List.mem_range.2 hq₀.lt) hq x hx
  unfold EndUseAnchorOK OptP at hc; rw [hy] at hc
  obtain ⟨hnh, -, hl⟩ := hc
  exact ⟨y, by rw [endUseEff, cleanup_get, endUseS_get, hy]; simp [hnh, hl], ya⟩

/-- `endUse` preserves `NoDangling` (§54, §69), under `WF3` (§49) and `RootHeldConv` (§40): an
active authority on a leaf of a place that stops being usable is derived, and blocked by §69.2, or
a root, held by the owner of the root place of the leaf, which would stay usable. -/
theorem EndFree.endUse_noDangling {k : K} {s : S3} {p : Nat} (hw : WF3 s) (hnd : NoDangling s)
    (ha : RootHeldConv s) (hpre : EndUsePre k s p) (hw' : WF3 (endUseEff s p)) :
    NoDangling (endUseEff s p) := by
  have hU := cleanup_usable (endUseS s p)
  intro j z hz za q hq l hl hlz
  obtain ⟨hz₀, hnh, hlive⟩ := endUse_active hz za
  by_cases hq₀ : ¬ s.Usable q
  · exact hnd j z hz₀ za q hq₀ l hl hlz
  replace hq₀ := Decidable.of_not_not hq₀
  obtain ⟨-, hleaf, hlq⟩ := mem_footprint.1 hl
  have hl₀ : s.Usable l := usable_of_partOf hw (l + 1) l q (Nat.lt_succ_self l) hlq hq₀
  have hl₁ : ¬ (endUseS s p).Usable l := fun hu => hq (usable_of_part hw' hlq ((hU l).2 hu))
  cases hzo : z.origin with
  | some o =>
    have hacc := hpre.access j (List.mem_range.2 (lt_of_getElem? hz₀))
    unfold EndUseAccessOK OptP at hacc; rw [hz₀] at hacc
    rcases hacc za (by rw [hzo]; simp) ⟨l, hlz, .inr ⟨hleaf, hl₀, hl₁⟩⟩ with e | e
    · exact hnh e
    · exact e hlive
  | none =>
    obtain ⟨-, -, r, -, -, -, hr, hlr, -⟩ := hw.rootChain j z l hz₀ hlz hleaf
    obtain ⟨pr, hpr, hh⟩ := ha j z l r hz₀ hzo hlz hr hlr
    have hnown : ¬ OwnedIn s.P p r := fun hown => by
      cases hown with
      | @direct _ o _ hpl ho hpart =>
        have e : pr.owner = .place o := by rw [hpr] at hpl; cases hpl; exact ho
        rw [hh, e] at hnh; exact hnh hpart
      | @step _ o _ hpl ho hown' =>
        have e : pr.owner = .place o := by rw [hpr] at hpl; cases hpl; exact ho
        rw [hh, e] at hlive
        have := dead_false hlive
        simp only [endUseS, Bool.or_eq_false_iff, decide_eq_false_iff_not] at this
        exact this.2 hown'
    have hd : (endUseS s p).dead r = false := by
      simp only [endUseS, ← hw.deadOf hlr, dead_false hl₀, Bool.false_or,
        decide_eq_false_iff_not]
      exact hnown
    have hr₁ : (endUseS s p).Usable r := usable_of_owner hpr hd (hh ▸ hlive)
    exact hl₁ ((hU l).1 (usable_of_partOf hw' (l + 1) l r (Nat.lt_succ_self l) hlr ((hU r).2 hr₁)))

import Ern.MemoryModel.Access.Preserve.Common

/-!
# Access kernel: preservation by `enterFrame` and `exitFrame`

Operations O6 `enterFrame` (§72) and O7 `exitFrame` (§73) of
`specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.md`, with the frame rules of §39 and the parameter and
reanchoring rules of §45. Both steps preserve the kernel invariant of §57 (`KInv`) together with
the auxiliary invariant `KAux`. The file also proves entry protection of parameters (§72.3 and
the last paragraph of §72), the release of authorities whose holder dies at the exit (§73
effect, §39), the absence of dangling authorities after the exit (§73, §54), reanchoring to the
first surviving active origin (§73.4, §73 effect), and determinism of both steps (§58).

Helper lemmas live in the namespace `Ern.MemoryModel.Access.Frames`.
-/

namespace Ern.MemoryModel.Access

namespace Frames

/-! ## Lists -/

/-- Indices of `List.range` are strictly increasing (§72: identities of the root locals). -/
theorem range_pairwise_lt : ∀ n, (List.range n).Pairwise (· < ·)
  | 0 => by simp
  | n + 1 => by
    rw [List.range_succ, List.pairwise_append]
    refine ⟨range_pairwise_lt n, List.pairwise_singleton _ _, fun a ha b hb => ?_⟩
    rw [List.mem_singleton] at hb; subst hb; exact List.mem_range.1 ha

/-- In a strictly increasing list, a value sits at one index only (§72: identities of the root
locals). -/
theorem getElem?_inj_of_lt : ∀ {l : List Nat} {i j x : Nat}, l.Pairwise (· < ·) →
    l[i]? = some x → l[j]? = some x → i = j
  | [], _, _, _, _, h, _ => by simp at h
  | _ :: _, 0, 0, _, _, _, _ => rfl
  | _ :: l, 0, j + 1, x, hp, hi, hj => by
    simp only [List.getElem?_cons_zero, Option.some.injEq] at hi; subst hi
    have := (List.pairwise_cons.1 hp).1 _ (List.mem_of_getElem? hj)
    exact absurd this (Nat.lt_irrefl _)
  | _ :: l, i + 1, 0, x, hp, hi, hj => by
    simp only [List.getElem?_cons_zero, Option.some.injEq] at hj; subst hj
    have := (List.pairwise_cons.1 hp).1 _ (List.mem_of_getElem? hi)
    exact absurd this (Nat.lt_irrefl _)
  | _ :: l, i + 1, j + 1, x, hp, hi, hj => by
    simp only [List.getElem?_cons_succ] at hi hj
    rw [getElem?_inj_of_lt (List.pairwise_cons.1 hp).2 hi hj]

/-- A member of a list sits at some index (§72: the root locals). -/
theorem exists_getElem?_of_mem {α : Type} {a : α} : ∀ {l : List α}, a ∈ l →
    ∃ k : Nat, l[k]? = some a
  | b :: l, h => by
    rcases List.mem_cons.1 h with rfl | h
    · exact ⟨0, rfl⟩
    · obtain ⟨k, hk⟩ := exists_getElem?_of_mem h; exact ⟨k + 1, by simpa using hk⟩

/-- An element of the mapped suffix of an appended list has an index (§72: the root authorities
of the locals). -/
theorem append_map_get {α β : Type} (A₀ : List β) (g : α → β) {l : List α} {a : α} (h : a ∈ l) :
    ∃ j, (A₀ ++ l.map g)[A₀.length + j]? = some (g a) := by

end Frames

/-! ## Preservation of the kernel invariant (§57, §72, §73) -/

/-- `enterFrame` preserves the kernel invariant of §57 (`WF3 ∧ Inv3 ∧ AnchorOrderHeld ∧
NoOrphan`) and the auxiliary `RootHeldConv` (§72). -/
theorem enter_preserves {s s' : S3} {ps : List Nat} {ls : LocalShape} (hk : KInv s)
    (ha : KAux s) (h : EnterStep ps ls s (.ok s')) : KInv s' ∧ KAux s' := by
  obtain ⟨hpre, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h
  obtain ⟨hwf, ⟨hb, hao, hnd⟩, -, -⟩ := hk
  exact ⟨kInv_of (Frames.enter_wf hwf hpre) ⟨Frames.enter_inv3base hwf hb,
    Frames.enter_anchorOrder hwf hao hpre, Frames.enter_noDangling hwf hnd hpre⟩
    hpre.anchorOrderHeld, Frames.enter_rootHeldConv hwf hpre ha⟩

/-- `exitFrame` preserves the kernel invariant of §57 (`WF3 ∧ Inv3 ∧ AnchorOrderHeld ∧
NoOrphan`) and the auxiliary `RootHeldConv` (§73). -/
theorem exit_preserves {k : K} {s s' : S3} (hk : KInv s) (ha : KAux s)
    (h : ExitStep k s (.ok s')) : KInv s' ∧ KAux s' := by
  obtain ⟨hpre, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h
  obtain ⟨hwf, ⟨hb, hao, hnd⟩, -, -⟩ := hk
  exact ⟨kInv_of (Frames.exit_wf hwf hpre.hasCaller hpre.origins)
    ⟨Frames.exit_inv3base hb hpre.anchors,
     Frames.exit_anchorOrder hwf hao hpre.anchors hpre.origins,
     Frames.exit_noDangling hwf hnd ha hpre.origins⟩ hpre.anchorOrderHeld,
    Frames.exit_rootHeldConv ha hpre.origins⟩

/-! ## Determinism (§58, §72, §73) -/

/-- `enterFrame` has one outcome (§58, §72). -/
theorem enterStep_det {s : S3} {ps : List Nat} {ls : LocalShape} {o₁ o₂ : Outcome3 S3}
    (h₁ : EnterStep ps ls s o₁) (h₂ : EnterStep ps ls s o₂) : o₁ = o₂ :=
  Guarded.det h₁ h₂

/-- `exitFrame` has one outcome (§58, §73). -/
theorem exitStep_det {k : K} {s : S3} {o₁ o₂ : Outcome3 S3} (h₁ : ExitStep k s o₁)
    (h₂ : ExitStep k s o₂) : o₁ = o₂ :=
  Guarded.det h₁ h₂

/-! ## Frames (§39) -/

/-- Neither step changes the bottom of the stack (§39: the base frame never exits): `exitFrame`
keeps a nonempty stack with the same last frame. -/
theorem exit_keeps_base {k : K} {s s' : S3} (h : ExitStep k s (.ok s')) :
    s'.F ≠ [] ∧ s'.F.getLast? = s.F.getLast? := by
  obtain ⟨hpre, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h
  refine ⟨hpre.hasCaller, ?_⟩
  show s.F.tail.getLast? = s.F.getLast?
  cases hF : s.F with
  | nil => rfl
  | cons f F₀ => exact (getLast?_cons_ne (by simpa [hF] using hpre.hasCaller)).symm

/-- Neither step changes the bottom of the stack (§39: the base frame never exits):
`enterFrame` pushes the new frame on top. -/
theorem enter_keeps_base {s s' : S3} {ps : List Nat} {ls : LocalShape}
    (h : EnterStep ps ls s (.ok s')) : s'.F.getLast? = s.F.getLast? := by
  obtain ⟨hpre, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h
  exact getLast?_cons_ne hpre.callerLive

/-- An exited frame leaves the stack and is the terminal owner of no usable place (§39, §73 `ok`
effect, first item). -/
theorem exitFrame_frame_gone {k : K} {s s' : S3} (hw : WF3 s) (h : ExitStep k s (.ok s')) :
    s.top ∉ s'.F ∧ ∀ q, s'.Usable q → ¬ FrameOf s' q s.top := by
  obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h
  obtain ⟨f, F₀, hF⟩ : ∃ f F₀, s.F = f :: F₀ := by
    cases h : s.F with
    | nil => exact absurd h hw.frames.1
    | cons f F₀ => exact ⟨f, F₀, rfl⟩
  have hnd := (List.nodup_cons.1 (hF ▸ hw.frames.2.1)).1
  have htop : s.top = f := by simp [S3.top, hF]
  have hF' : (exitEff s).F = F₀ := by simp [exitEff, hF]
  rw [htop, hF']
  refine ⟨hnd, fun q hq hfq => ?_⟩
  obtain ⟨g, hg, hgF⟩ := hq.frameOf
  have e := FrameOf.det hfq hg
  rw [hF', ← e] at hgF
  exact hnd hgF

/-! ## Release at the exit (§73 `ok` effect, §39, §45) -/

/-- `exitFrame_releases_all` (§73 `ok` effect, second item; §39; §45): after an `ok` exit, an
authority held by the exited frame or by a place that is no longer usable is released, with its
holder unchanged (it is not returned to the caller); every active authority has a live holder,
other than the exited frame. -/
theorem exitFrame_releases_all {k : K} {s s' : S3} (hw : WF3 s) (h : ExitStep k s (.ok s')) :
    (∀ (j : Nat) (y : Authority), s.A[j]? = some y →
      (y.holder = .frame s.top ∨ ∃ p, y.holder = .place p ∧ ¬ s'.Usable p) →
      ∃ y', s'.A[j]? = some y' ∧ y'.active = false ∧ y'.holder = y.holder) ∧
    (∀ (j : Nat) (y : Authority), s'.A[j]? = some y → y.active = true →
      HolderLive s' y.holder ∧ y.holder ≠ .frame s.top) := by
  obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h
  obtain ⟨f, F₀, hF⟩ : ∃ f F₀, s.F = f :: F₀ := by
    cases h : s.F with
    | nil => exact absurd h hw.frames.1
    | cons f F₀ => exact ⟨f, F₀, rfl⟩
  have hnd := (List.nodup_cons.1 (hF ▸ hw.frames.2.1)).1
  have htop : s.top = f := by simp [S3.top, hF]
  have hlive : ∀ hd, HolderLive (exitEff s) hd ↔ HolderLive ({ s with F := s.F.tail } : S3) hd :=
    HolderLive.congr (s := ({ s with F := s.F.tail } : S3)) (s' := exitEff s) rfl rfl rfl
  have hnot : ¬ HolderLive ({ s with F := s.F.tail } : S3) (.frame f) := by
    show f ∉ s.F.tail; rw [hF]; exact hnd
  refine ⟨fun j y hy hh => ?_, fun j y hy ya => ?_⟩
  · have hns : ¬ Survives s s.F.tail j := by
      unfold Survives; rw [hy]; rintro ⟨-, hl⟩
      rcases hh with e | ⟨p, e, hp⟩
      · rw [e, htop] at hl; exact hnot hl

  · obtain ⟨y₀, hy₀, rfl⟩ := Frames.exit_get hy
    have hs := Frames.exitG_active ya
    unfold Survives at hs; rw [hy₀] at hs
    have hl : HolderLive ({ s with F := s.F.tail } : S3) y₀.holder := hs.2
    rw [(Frames.exitG_same s s.F.tail j y₀).2.2]

/-! ## No dangling authority after the exit (§73, §54) -/

/-- `exitFrame_no_dangling` (§73, §54): after an `ok` exit, no active authority covers a leaf of
a place that is not usable, in particular of a local of the exited frame or of storage dying with
it. -/
theorem exitFrame_no_dangling {k : K} {s s' : S3} (hw : WF3 s) (hnd : NoDangling s)
    (hc : RootHeldConv s) (h : ExitStep k s (.ok s')) :
    ∀ q, ¬ s'.Usable q → ∀ (j : Nat) (y : Authority), s'.A[j]? = some y → y.active = true →
      ∀ l ∈ footprint s'.P q, l ∉ y.footprint := by
  obtain ⟨hpre, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h
  intro q hq j y hy ya
  exact Frames.exit_noDangling hw hnd hc hpre.origins j y hy ya q hq

/-! ## Reanchoring at the exit (§73.4, §73 `ok` effect, §45) -/

/-- Reanchoring (§73.4; §73 `ok` effect, third and fourth items; §45): after an `ok` exit, a
surviving authority stays active with its own mode, footprint and holder; it keeps no origin if
it had none; otherwise its origin becomes the first surviving active origin of its chain: no
earlier ancestor survives, and that origin is active and held, after the exit, by a frame of the
stack or by a usable place. -/
theorem exitFrame_reanchors {k : K} {s s' : S3} (h : ExitStep k s (.ok s')) {a : Nat}
    {y : Authority} (hy : s.A[a]? = some y) (hs : Survives s s.F.tail a) :
    ∃ y', s'.A[a]? = some y' ∧ y'.active = true ∧ y'.mode = y.mode ∧
      y'.footprint = y.footprint ∧ y'.holder = y.holder ∧
      (y.origin = none → y'.origin = none) ∧
      (y.origin ≠ none → ∃ (z : Nat) (pre post : List Nat) (yz : Authority),
        y'.origin = some z ∧ s.ancs a = pre ++ z :: post ∧
        (∀ w ∈ pre, ¬ Survives s s.F.tail w) ∧
        s'.A[z]? = some yz ∧ yz.active = true ∧ HolderLive s' yz.holder) := by
  obtain ⟨hpre, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h
  have hlive : ∀ hd, HolderLive (exitEff s) hd ↔ HolderLive ({ s with F := s.F.tail } : S3) hd :=
    HolderLive.congr (s := ({ s with F := s.F.tail } : S3)) (s' := exitEff s) rfl rfl rfl
  obtain ⟨ym, yf, yh⟩ := Frames.exitG_same s s.F.tail a y
  refine ⟨_, by rw [Frames.exit_A_get, hy]; rfl, Frames.exitG_surv hy hs, ym, yf, yh,
    fun ho => by simp [exitG, hs, ho], fun ho => ?_⟩
  have horg : s.org a ≠ none := by simpa [S3.org, hy] using ho
  obtain ⟨z, hz⟩ := Option.ne_none_iff_exists'.1
    (hpre.origins a (List.mem_range.2 (lt_of_getElem? hy)) hs horg)
  obtain ⟨-, pre, post, hl, hpre'⟩ := List.find?_eq_some_iff_append.1 hz
  obtain ⟨-, hzs⟩ := Frames.firstSurv_some hz
  have hzs' := hzs
  unfold Survives OptP at hzs'
  split at hzs'
  · rename_i yz hyz
    refine ⟨z, pre, post, _, ?_, hl, fun w hw => by simpa using hpre' w hw,
      by rw [Frames.exit_A_get, hyz]; rfl, Frames.exitG_surv hyz hzs, ?_⟩
    · obtain ⟨o, ho'⟩ := Option.ne_none_iff_exists'.1 ho
      simp [exitG, hs, ho', hz]
    · rw [(Frames.exitG_same s s.F.tail z yz).2.2]; exact (hlive _).2 hzs'.2
  · exact hzs'.elim

/-- Reanchoring of anchors (§73 `ok` effect, third item; §73.5): after an `ok` exit, every anchor
of a usable place is replaced by the first surviving authority among itself and its origins,
which is an anchor of the place after the exit and is active. -/
theorem exitFrame_reanchors_anchors {k : K} {s s' : S3} (h : ExitStep k s (.ok s')) :
    ∀ q, s'.Usable q → ∀ x ∈ s.D q, ∃ z, firstSurv s s.F.tail (x :: s.ancs x) = some z ∧
      (z = x ∨ z ∈ s.ancs x) ∧ z ∈ s'.D q ∧ s'.Active z := by
  obtain ⟨hpre, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h
  intro q hq x hx
  have hq₁ : ({ s with F := s.F.tail } : S3).Usable q := Frames.exit_usable_iff.1 hq
  have hne := hpre.anchors q (List.mem_range.2 (Frames.usable_of_tail hq₁).lt) hq₁ x hx
  obtain ⟨z, hz⟩ := Option.ne_none_iff_exists'.1 hne
  obtain ⟨hzm, hzs⟩ := Frames.firstSurv_some hz
  have hmem : z ∈ (exitEff s).D q := List.mem_map.2 ⟨x, hx, by simp [hz]⟩
  refine ⟨z, hz, List.mem_cons.1 hzm, hmem, ?_⟩
  have hzs' := hzs
  unfold Survives OptP at hzs'
  split at hzs'
  · rename_i yz hyz
    exact ⟨_, by rw [Frames.exit_A_get, hyz]; rfl, Frames.exitG_surv hyz hzs⟩
  · exact hzs'.elim

/-! ## Parameters (§45, §72) -/

/-- The caller yields its parameters (§45; §72 `ok` effect): after an `ok` entry the new frame is
the current frame, it holds every parameter, the other existing authorities are unchanged, and
every new authority is the root authority (no origin) of a root local, held by the new frame, so
the caller keeps no copy of a parameter. -/
theorem enter_yields {s s' : S3} {ps : List Nat} {ls : LocalShape} (hw : WF3 s)
    (h : EnterStep ps ls s (.ok s')) :
    s'.top = s.nF ∧ s.nF ∉ s.F ∧ s'.F = s.nF :: s.F ∧
    (∀ j < s.A.length, s'.A[j]? =
      (s.A[j]?).map fun y => if j ∈ ps then { y with holder := .frame s'.top } else y) ∧
    (∀ (j : Nat) (y : Authority), s.A.length ≤ j → s'.A[j]? = some y →
      y.origin = none ∧ y.holder = .frame s'.top) := by
  obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h
  have htop : (enterEff s ps ls).top = s.nF := rfl
  refine ⟨htop, ?_, rfl, fun j hj => by rw [htop]; exact Frames.enter_lt hj,
    fun j y hj hy => ?_⟩
  · exact fun hm => Nat.lt_irrefl _ (hw.frames.2.2 _ hm)
  · rcases Frames.enter_get hy with ⟨hj', -⟩ | ⟨-, i, -, rfl⟩
    · omega
    · exact ⟨rfl, rfl⟩

/-- An active `Modify` authority takes every effective mode, on each of its leaves, away from its
direct origin (§43 case 3; last paragraph of §72: while a `Modify` parameter remains active, its
direct origin remains subject to effective-mode restrictions). -/
theorem param_origin_restricted {s : S3} (hw : WF3 s) {p o l : Nat} {y : Authority}
    (hp : s.A[p]? = some y) (ya : y.active = true) (hm : y.mode = .modify)
    (ho : y.origin = some o) (hl : l ∈ y.footprint) : effective s o l = none := by
  have hop : s.org p = some o := by simp [S3.org, hp, ho]
  have hoa : o ∈ s.ancs p := by
    rw [S3.ancs, chain_cons hop (hw.origins p y o hp ho)]; exact List.mem_cons_self ..
  have hd : Mode.modify ∈ descModes s o l := mem_descModes.2 ⟨p, y, hp, ya, hl, hoa, hm⟩
  unfold effective
  split
  · split
    · unfold effOf
      have hne : descModes s o l ≠ [] := fun e => by rw [e] at hd; cases hd
      simp [hne, hd]
    · rfl
  · rfl

/-- While an active `Modify` authority `p` covers a leaf, every authority with a present
effective mode on that leaf is `p` or one of its descendants (§50 `I1`, §43; last paragraph of
§72 for a `Modify` parameter). -/
theorem call_params_effective_protected {s : S3} (h1 : I1 s) {p b l : Nat} {y : Authority}
    (hp : s.A[p]? = some y) (ya : y.active = true) (hm : y.mode = .modify) (hl : l ∈ y.footprint)
    (hb : effective s b l ≠ none) : b = p ∨ p ∈ s.ancs b := by
  by_cases e : b = p
  · exact .inl e
  by_cases hpb : p ∈ s.ancs b
  · exact .inr hpb
  cases he : effective s b l with
  | none => exact absurd he hb
  | some mb =>
    obtain ⟨x, hx, xa, xl, ex⟩ := effective_some he
    by_cases hbp : b ∈ s.ancs p
    · have hd : Mode.modify ∈ descModes s b l := mem_descModes.2 ⟨p, y, hp, ya, hl, hbp, hm⟩
      rcases effOf_cases ex with ⟨h0, -⟩ | ⟨-, hn, -⟩
      · simp [h0] at hd
      · exact absurd hd hn
    · have := (h1 b p x y l e hx hp xa ya xl hl hbp hpb).2
      rw [hm] at this; cases this

/-- `enter_params_protected` (§72.3; last paragraph of §72): after an `ok` entry, the direct
origin of each `Modify` parameter is exercisable in no mode, and on each leaf of a `Modify`
parameter every authority with a present effective mode is the parameter or one of its
descendants, so its direct origin has no effective mode there. -/
theorem enter_params_protected {s s' : S3} {ps : List Nat} {ls : LocalShape} (hwf : WF3 s)
    (h1 : I1 s) (h : EnterStep ps ls s (.ok s')) :
    (∀ p ∈ ps, ParamOriginHidden s' p) ∧
      ∀ p ∈ ps, ∀ y : Authority, s'.A[p]? = some y → y.mode = .modify → ∀ l ∈ y.footprint,
        (∀ b, effective s' b l ≠ none → b = p ∨ p ∈ s'.ancs b) ∧
        ∀ o, y.origin = some o → effective s' o l = none := by
  obtain ⟨hpre, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h
  have hi1 := Frames.enter_i1 hwf h1 (ps := ps) (ls := ls)
  have hwf' := Frames.enter_wf hwf hpre
  refine ⟨hpre.originHidden, fun p hp y hy hm l hl => ?_⟩
  have ya : y.active = true := by
    have h2 := hpre.params p hp
    unfold OptP at h2; split at h2
    · rename_i y₀ hy₀
      rw [Frames.enter_lt (lt_of_getElem? hy₀), hy₀] at hy
      simp only [Option.map_some, Option.some.injEq] at hy
      subst hy; split <;> exact h2.1
    · exact h2.elim
  exact ⟨fun b hb => call_params_effective_protected hi1 hy ya hm hl hb,
    fun o ho => param_origin_restricted hwf' hy ya hm ho hl⟩

/-! ## Witness: reanchoring to an origin held by a place (§73.4) -/

namespace Frames.Witness

open Examples

/-- After `derive(0, [0], Modify)` (authority 3) and `store(3, 1)` (§60, §65): authority 3 is
held by static place 1. -/
def w2 : S3 := storeEff s1 3 1
/-- After `derive(3, [0], Modify)` (§60): authority 4, held by frame 0. -/
def w3 : S3 := deriveEff w2 3 [0] .modify
/-- After `derive(2, [2], Modify)` (§60): authority 5, held by frame 0. -/
def w4 : S3 := deriveEff w3 2 [2] .modify
/-- After `enterFrame([4, 5], [])` (§72): frame 1 holds parameters 4 and 5. -/
def w5 : S3 := enterEff w4 [4, 5] []
/-- After `derive(4, [0], Modify)` (§60): authority 6, held by frame 1. -/
def w6 : S3 := deriveEff w5 4 [0] .modify
/-- After `store(6, 2)` (§65): authority 6 is held by static place 2, owned by frame 0. -/
def w7 : S3 := storeEff w6 6 2

/-- The state `w7` is reachable from `S3.init st` (§57). -/
theorem w7_reachable : Reachable K0 st w7 :=
  .step (.step (.step (.step (.step (.step (.step .init
    (.derive (.ok (by decide : DerivePre s0 0 [0] .modify))))
    (.store (.ok (by decide : StorePre s1 3 1))))
    (.derive (.ok (by decide : DerivePre w2 3 [0] .modify))))
    (.derive (.ok (by decide : DerivePre w3 2 [2] .modify))))
    (.enter (.ok (by decide : EnterPre w4 [4, 5] []))))
    (.derive (.ok (by decide : DerivePre w5 4 [0] .modify))))
    (.store (.ok (by decide : StorePre w6 6 2)))

/-- Witness for §73.4 (a surviving origin is not skipped because it is held by a place): from
the reachable state `w7`, `exitFrame` is `ok`; authority 6 (held by place 2) survives; its
direct origin 4, held by the exiting frame, does not survive; it is reanchored to authority 3,
the next origin of its chain, which is active and held by the usable place 1, rather than to the
root authority 0. -/
theorem exit_reanchors_to_place_witness :
    Reachable K0 st w7 ∧ ExitStep K0 w7 (.ok (exitEff w7)) ∧
      w7.org 6 = some 4 ∧ w7.org 4 = some 3 ∧ w7.org 3 = some 0 ∧
      Survives w7 w7.F.tail 6 ∧ ¬ Survives w7 w7.F.tail 4 ∧
      (exitEff w7).org 6 = some 3 ∧
      OptP ((exitEff w7).A[3]?) (fun z => z.active = true ∧ z.holder = .place 1) False ∧
      (exitEff w7).Usable 1 :=
  ⟨w7_reachable, .ok (by decide), by decide, by decide, by decide, by decide, by decide,
    by decide, by decide, by decide⟩

end Frames.Witness

/-- `effective_exclusive` (§50): under `I1`, an authority with effective `Modify` on a leaf is the
only one with a present effective mode there. -/
theorem effective_exclusive {s : S3} (h : I1 s) {a b p : Nat} (hab : a ≠ b)
    (ha : effective s a p = some .modify) : effective s b p = none := by
  cases hb : effective s b p with
  | none => rfl
  | some m => exact absurd (effective_compat h a b p _ _ hab ha hb).1 (by simp)

/-- Compatibility of effective modes is symmetric (§50). -/
theorem Compat.symm {m₁ m₂ : Mode} (h : Compat m₁ m₂) : Compat m₂ m₁ := ⟨h.2, h.1⟩

/-- `I4` holds in every state (§53, first sentence): a read requires `Init` on every leaf read
(§66.1). -/
theorem i4_always (s : S3) : I4 s := fun _ _ l hl hm h => by rw [h.init l hl] at hm; cases hm

/-! ## Additions of authorities (§42, §60, §61) -/

/-- A list whose members are none is empty (§43, §63.2). -/
theorem nil_of_forall_not_mem {α : Type} : ∀ {l : List α}, (∀ a, a ∉ l) → l = []
  | [], _ => rfl
  | a :: _, h => absurd (List.mem_cons_self ..) (h a)

/-- `filterMap` depends only on the values of the function on the list (§43, `descModes`). -/
theorem filterMap_congr' {α β : Type} {f g : α → Option β} :
    ∀ {l : List α}, (∀ a ∈ l, f a = g a) → l.filterMap f = l.filterMap g
  | [], _ => rfl
  | a :: l, h => by
    simp only [List.filterMap_cons, h a (List.mem_cons_self ..),
      filterMap_congr' fun b hb => h b (List.mem_cons_of_mem a hb)]

/-- The authorities after an addition: the former ones, and the new one at the fresh identity
(§42, fresh identities). -/
theorem addAuth_get {s : S3} {y₀ z : Authority} {j : Nat} (h : (s.addAuth y₀).A[j]? = some z) :
    (j < s.A.length ∧ s.A[j]? = some z) ∨ (j = s.A.length ∧ z = y₀) := by
  simp only [S3.addAuth] at h
  by_cases hj : j < s.A.length
  · exact .inl ⟨hj, by rwa [List.getElem?_append_left hj] at h⟩
  · rw [List.getElem?_append_right (by omega)] at h

/-- Decidability of `OwnedIn` (§40). -/
instance (P : List Place) (src q : Nat) : Decidable (OwnedIn P src q) :=
  decidable_of_iff _ ownedIn_iff.symm

/-! ## Effective modes (§43) -/

/-- Modes of the active descendants of `a` whose footprint covers leaf `p` (§43). -/
def descModes (s : S3) (a p : Nat) : List Mode :=
  (List.range s.A.length).filterMap fun j =>
    match s.A[j]? with
    | some y => if y.active = true ∧ p ∈ y.footprint ∧ a ∈ s.ancs j then some y.mode else none
    | none => none

/-- Cases 2–4 of §43 for an active authority of own mode `m` covering the leaf, whose covering
active descendants have modes `ds`. -/
def effOf (m : Mode) (ds : List Mode) : Option Mode :=
  if ds = [] then some m else if Mode.modify ∈ ds then none else some .observe

/-- `effective(s, a, l)` (§43, cases 1–4), computed per leaf. -/
def effective (s : S3) (a p : Nat) : Option Mode :=
  match s.A[a]? with
  | some x => if x.active = true ∧ p ∈ x.footprint then effOf x.mode (descModes s a p) else none
  | none => none

/-- Compatible effective modes for independent ordinary accesses: only `Observe`/`Observe`
(§50). -/
def Compat (m₁ m₂ : Mode) : Prop := m₁ = .observe ∧ m₂ = .observe

/-- Effective mode `e` permits the requested mode `m`: present and not exceeded (§43). -/
def Allows (e : Option Mode) (m : Mode) : Prop := OptP e (fun e => m.le e) False

/-- Decidability of `Allows` (§43). -/
instance (e : Option Mode) (m : Mode) : Decidable (Allows e m) := by
  unfold Allows; infer_instance

/-- Footprint of authority `a` (§42), empty if it does not exist. -/
def S3.afp (s : S3) (a : Nat) : List Nat := match s.A[a]? with
  | some x => x.footprint
  | none => []

/-- Adds an authority with fresh identity `s.A.length` (§42, §60). -/
def S3.addAuth (s : S3) (y : Authority) : S3 := { s with A := s.A ++ [y] }

/-! ## Exercisable authorities (§43) -/

/-- `ExercisableAt(s, a, m)` (§43): `a` is active, its own mode permits `m`, and it is held by
the current frame, or by a place `p` such that an authority itself exercisable at `m` has an
effective mode permitting `m` on every leaf of `p`. Inductive along the holder chain (§43), so no
holder cycle justifies a right. -/
inductive S3.ExercisableAt (s : S3) : Nat → Mode → Prop where

    carry `m.le y.mode`.

    leafhood, and §49.7 (via RootHeld.transport).
- **Transfer shape (§63)**: transfer_P_get, transfer_A_get, transfer_len, transfer_parentOf,
  transfer_footprint, transfer_partOf, mem_kids, kids_nil_iff, corrF_fuel, corr_src, corr_step,

  read `D`, so the new `D` effect does not affect them.

  getLast?_append_single, getLast?_dropWhile, length_dropWhile_le, dropWhile_ne_of_mem,
  dropLoops (def), mem_dropLoops, dropLoops_head, dropLoops_ne_nil, dropLoops_getLast,

  - `rootLive_cover` is now **rootHeld_cover**. It reads `hw.rootHeld` and ignores the mode.

    separate RootLive hypothesis any more.

## Dropped, and why

- `RootsDisjoint`, `rootsDisjoint_always`: the kernel has no `RootsDisjoint`, and WF3 has no such
  field. Its content survives as `rootOf_unique`.
- `pairwise_lt_range`: the brief forbids it (Classical.choice). In the draft only the `split`
  preservation proofs use it, so the split agent needs a choice-free replacement.
- `shared_keeps_exclusivity`: it restates I1 verbatim (§50) and is not a shared lemma.
- `write3_exclusive`: it is specific to one operation. `Write3Pre.exclusive` (§67.2) now gives
  it directly.
- The positional projections (WF3.origin/fp/ne/nodup/frames/ownerFrame/ownerPlace/parts/poss/
  rootChain/rootHeld) are replaced by the structure fields: `origins`, `footprints`,
  `frames.1/.2.1/.2.2`, `owners.1/.2.1`, `places`, `holders`, `rootChain`, `rootHeld`.
- `RootLive`: this is now `WF3.rootHeld` (plus the mode).
- `transfer_rootHeld`: it preserves the converse (`RootHeldConv`) under transfer. That is a
  preservation proof, left to the transfer agent; the draft proof should port verbatim.
- All `*_preserves` proofs, `split_aux`, the RootLive preservation section
  (`exists_getElem?_of_mem` …) and the `Inv3.*` projections are out of scope.

None.

## Observations for arbitration (no lemma blocked)

1. **The third conjunct of WF3.owners holds in every state.** For every usable place, it requires
   ownership chains that are well-founded and reach a live frame (§49.3). `S3.Usable.frameOf`
   proves this in every state, without WF3, because `Usable` is inductive. The field therefore
   adds nothing beyond the inductive reading of §40.
2. **NoOrphan follows from WF3 alone** (`noOrphan_of_wf3`, using §49.2, §49.7 and §49.8). Under
   these definitions, the `NoOrphan` conjunct of §57 is redundant given `WF3`. The argument
   matches §54 and does not rely on a permissive definition.
3. **Suggested lemma, not added because it is outside the brief.** `ExercisableAt a m → ∃ y,
   s.A[a]? = some y ∧ y.active ∧ m.le y.mode` would discharge `hm` for derive and split.

## Obligations not proved (false), with counterexamples

1. **Preservation of `KInv ∧ KAux` by §63 as written: FALSE.** `transfer_breaks_kinv`. Statics

   by 0, root 2 held by 0; `alloc(provider 1, owner 2, [(none,0)])` → place 3 owned by 2, root 3
   held by 2 (`cyc2`, reachable, `KInv ∧ KAux` decided). `TransferPre K0 cyc2 0 3` decided (all
   eight clauses, §63.8 included). In `cyc3`, places 2 and 3 own each other; root 2 is active,
   held by unusable place 3 (§49.8 fails) and covers leaf 2 of unusable place 2 (`NoDangling`
   fails). `DDSound K0` holds, so this refutes §57 under its own hypothesis. Same as SP-A1 / P1 /
   P6 of the readings and maps, now machine-checked in the module.

2. **`transfer_preserves_of_dst_usable` (`KInv ∧ KAux` + destination usable after ⇒ `KInv' ∧
   KAux'`): FALSE as an implication on `KInv ∧ KAux` states.** Failing invariant:
   `AnchorOrderHeld` (§44, §54); everything else holds
   (`transfer_preserves_wf3_inv3_of_dst_usable`). Cause: the literal quantifier of §63.7 ("All
   **moved** held authorities ... satisfy `AnchorOrderHeld` in the resulting state"). An
   authority held by a place outside the value, whose effective anchor (a root) is held by the
   source or by storage it owns, keeps its holder while its effective anchor's frame changes to
   the destination's; §63.7 does not look at it, and §63.6 `AnchorOrder` sees it only if it is an
   anchor. Counterexample `transfer_preserves_of_dst_usable_fails`, state `ahx`: frames `[1, 0]`;
   place 0 (frame 0), source 1 (owned by 0, `Init`), place 2 (frame 0), place 3 (owned by 1),
   destination 4 (frame 1); roots 0–4; authority 5 derived from root 0 held by frame 1 (gives
   `Modify` on the source through place 0, so §63.4 is not triggered); authority 6 derived from
   root 3, held by place 2, `D` empty. `transfer(1, 4)` is accepted, 4 is usable after, and
   `AnchorOrderHeld` fails for authority 6 (effective anchor now held by 4 in frame 1, holder 2 in
   frame 0). **The state is not reached by kernel steps**: a derived authority is held by a place
   only through `store`, which also anchors it (`HeldAnchored` fails in `ahx`). I could not build
   a reachable counterexample.

   hypotheses named and documented as not spec clauses), plus `transfer_preserves_heldAnchored`
   (the extra hypothesis is preserved by `transfer` itself, with no condition).

   **Open**: whether `HeldAnchored` holds on every reachable state. Expected yes (`store` anchors
   what it stores; `release`, `endUse` deactivate what they unanchor; `exitFrame` maps a surviving
   anchor to itself; `derive`/`split`/`enterFrame` keep new or moved authorities frame-held;
   `alloc`/`enterFrame` roots have no origin), but each step's preservation is unproven, and it
   belongs to the per-operation modules. If it holds, the reachable form of obligation 2 holds.

- R1 "§63.8 is local": the decision of `NoLocalSelfLock` depends on the state only through `P`
  and the authorities held within `src` (the LockOptions statement, unchanged).
- R2 `transfer_invalidates_source`: "inaccessible as its former value" (§41) / "cannot be read"
  (§53) read as: no `Read3Pre s' a ls` for any `ls` containing the leaf (the reference `I4`).
- R3 `anchor_escape_rejected_at_transfer` keeps the draft hypothesis `a ∈ depsOf s src`; under the
  reference effect the anchor lands on `corr r`, and the rejection comes from §63.6
  `AnchorOrder (transferEff …)` at `corr r`.
- R4 `HeldAnchored` restricted to derived authorities (`origin ≠ none`) and usable holders: the
  weakest form the proof uses. Root authorities held by places are not anchors (alloc/enter roots)
  and need no hypothesis (a root is its own effective anchor).
- R5 `transfer_deps_follow` adds "no anchor appears from elsewhere" as a fourth conjunct: a
  property of the effect `transferEff` ("no authority is created or duplicated").

## Problems found (for arbitration)

- **P-T1 (= SP-A1, blocking §57 for transfer).** §63 admits an ownership cycle; machine-checked
  reachable counterexample `transfer_breaks_kinv`. Passages: §63 effect "places owned by `r`
  become owned by `corr(r)`"; §49.8; §54 `NoDangling`; §58 "An `ok` transition must ... preserve
  the relevant invariants". The draft's clause "destination usable in the resulting state" is
  sufficient for every invariant except the one in P-T2.
- **P-T2 (new).** §63.7 quotes "All moved held authorities, including those of owned storage,
  satisfy `AnchorOrderHeld` in the resulting state"; §44 "These conditions apply to the resulting
  states of operations that move or create holder relations". An unmoved held authority whose
  effective anchor moves is checked neither by §63.7 nor (if it is not an anchor) by §63.6.
  Example `ahx` above (`transfer_preserves_of_dst_usable_fails`). Harmless on reachable states if
  `HeldAnchored` is an invariant; otherwise needs §63.7 to cover every active authority held by a
  usable place of the resulting state (the draft's full `AnchorOrderHeld s'`).

- Per-clause rejection theorems of §63.1–§63.5 were not requested and not written.

- **Locals.** Locals are owned by `.frame s.nF` (`shapeOwner_toShape`). The draft `localOwner` machinery is
  dropped, and `enter_usable_new` is now one constructor with no induction.
- **§49.7 `RootHeld`.** The reference `RootHeld` is the draft `RootLive` plus the mode, so `enter_rootHeld` and
  `exit_rootHeld` port `enter_rootLive` and `exit_rootLive`. `RootHeld.transport` from Lemmas does not apply to
  the exit: it requires every active root authority to be unchanged, but the roots of the exiting frame's locals
  are released.
- **`RootHeldConv` (KAux).** This is the draft `RootHeld`. It is preserved by `enter_rootHeldConv` (an origin-free
  authority is never a parameter, and new roots are held by the frame that owns the local) and by
  `exit_rootHeldConv` (the `origins` precondition rules out a reanchored origin of `none`).
- **Exit NoDangling.** The proof is new and shorter than the draft's `OwnedByFrame` route. Take an active
  authority after the exit. Its chain root survives (§73.4) and, by `RootHeldConv`, is held by the owner of the
  root place of the leaf. That root place is therefore usable with the popped stack. So is every place
  containing the leaf, because §49.2 makes parts share the owner and death marker. KAux is used only here.
- **Dropped from the draft:**
  - `cleanup`/`OnlyReleases` (3751–3866), which serve endUse and free, not the exit.
  - `OwnedByFrame`, `exitFrame_kills_owned` and `exit_owned_of_usable`, now subsumed by
    `exitFrame_no_dangling` (NoDangling form) and `exitFrame_frame_gone`.
  - `exit_keeps_restrictions` and `dependent_cannot_escape_frame`, which the brief does not list.

## Readings taken (none changes an accepted program)

1. **§73/§54 `exitFrame_no_dangling`.** Read as NoDangling of the resulting state, for every unusable place
   (places that die with the frame are a special case). Hypotheses: `WF3`, `NoDangling` and `RootHeldConv`, all
   components of `KInv ∧ KAux`. The kernel-theorems map (`check/ND.lean`) reports that §49.7 WF3 and NoDangling
   alone do not suffice; `RootHeldConv` (or, per the map, I1) closes it.
2. **§73.4 "first surviving active origin".** Read through the reference `Survives` (active, and holder live with
   the popped stack). In `exitFrame_reanchors`, "first" is stated as a prefix decomposition
   `ancs a = pre ++ z :: post` with no surviving element in `pre`.
3. **§45 "sole holder" / "does not retain a copy".** Read as: the parameter's holder field becomes the new
   frame, and no new authority has an origin (`enter_yields`). "Not automatically returned to the caller" is
   read as: a non-surviving authority keeps its holder and becomes inactive (`exitFrame_releases_all`).
4. **§72 last paragraph** ("while a `Modify` parameter remains active, its direct origin remains subject to
   effective-mode restrictions"). Read as `effective s o l = none` on the parameter's leaves. This holds in every
   WF3 state (`param_origin_restricted`) and, under I1, extends to every non-descendant
   (`call_params_effective_protected`).
5. **§39 "the base frame never exits".** Proved per step only: enter and exit keep the last frame of the stack.
   That the last frame is 0 on reachable states needs an induction over all of O1–O16, which is outside this
   file.

## Problems found

- No definition blocked a proof, and there is no spec contradiction in scope.
- **§72.3 is a precondition.** `EnterPre.originHidden` is §72.3 itself, so the first conjunct of
  `enter_params_protected` is a projection (as in the draft). Only the effective-mode part carries content.
- **Not done (outside the brief list; suggested by `map/kernel-ops-b.md` B2(c)):**
  - a rejection witness for §73.4b (a surviving authority whose chain reaches only a root of the exiting frame);
  - an iff lemma for `ExitStep … .reject`;
  - a witness that `enter_preserves` needs `WF3` (the draft `enter_not_inv3_preserving`).
    Then derive 3 on x, store 3 into place 2, and derive 4 from 3, Observe on x.
    `FreePre K0 f3 2 0` holds, and after `free` authority 4 is active with origin 3 inactive.
  - Scratch file:
    `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-guygouri-Devlab-ernlang-ern/c986905c-e900-4fd9-bebc-4a3ce7ebb180/scratchpad/pres-end/W2.lean`.
    It is checked with `lake env lean` and prints no error.
  - Under the alternative reading "valid origin = active", I2 would fail on both witnesses. That
    is the open §51 arbitration, not a new problem.
- The **NoDangling** root case consumes `RootHeldConv` (KAux) and not I1. The derived case
  consumes only the `EndingLeaf`/`FreedLeaf` half of the access clause, which is the half the
  policy keeps.

## Readings taken (no new ones)

- I used the reference definitions as given: `endUseS`/`freeS` mark `OwnedIn` and `FreedPlace`
  dead, `freeS` leaves `D` unchanged, and `FreePre` has no `Usable p`. The policy's
  `EndingLeaf`/`FreedLeaf` scope applies.
- `endUse_pinned_reject` and `free_pinned_reject` are stated on the reference
  `EndingLeaf`/`FreedLeaf`.
- `endingLeaf_of_owned` and `freedLeaf_of_unit` connect them to the spec wording: leaves of `p`
  and of usable, transitively owned storage. A leaf of owned storage that was already unusable
  before the step is not an `EndingLeaf`, and §69.4 says "whose use ends".

## Observations (no proof blocked)

1. `endUse_place_usable` needs WF3. Without §49.2 (parts share the owner), `p` can be owned by its
   own part. Then `OwnedIn P p p` holds, and the effect marks `p` dead. So the §69 effect "`place`
   remains usable" depends on WF3. It is not a property of the effect alone.
2. On KInv states, `FreePre` implies `Usable p`, as the kernel-ops-b map notes. Every place has a
   leaf, and `HasRight .modify p` needs an active authority on it, so `NoDangling` forces `p`
   usable. No proof here uses this.
3. Of the draft theorems, `free_marks_freed` and `endUse_no_dealloc_event` read the removed
   `freed` field, so they are not ported. `free_no_pin` is the contrapositive of
   `free_pinned_reject`, since `pin` is unchanged by the effect, and is replaced by it.
   `endUse_rootLive` and `free_rootLive` are covered by the `rootHeld` field of WF3 inside
   `releases_preserve`.

# XV. Transitive Dependencies, Returns, and Value Behavior

Dependent values may survive transfers and calls only if the required anchors and rights remain valid. Second-class access does not imply an arbitrary persistent reference.

## 79. Non-Escaping Values and Returns

The second-class nature of access authorities does not prohibit constructing a value carrying a derived authority or returning a result dependent on a caller-owned resource. What is prohibited is artificially extending the validity of a local origin.

A typical scenario is:

```text
arena = create_arena()
buffer = create_buffer(arena)
use(buffer)
endUse(buffer)       // or equivalent release of its dependent rights
arena.reset()
```

The scenario is permitted when:

1. the call receives and exercises valid authorities over the arena;
2. issuance supplies a block disjoint from live issuances;
3. the result value is anchored to the rights actually required;
4. its transfer to the caller respects `SameShape`, holders, `AnchorOrder`, and `AnchorOrderHeld`;
5. `exitFrame` can reanchor surviving authorities without using a dead local root;
6. `reset` is rejected while the dependent result or a block authority remains active, then becomes permitted after those rights have effectively ended.

A “non-escaping” value is therefore not necessarily confined to the frame in which it was created. It may survive a function when it depends on a caller anchor, without extending dead local storage. This result does **not** imply strong protection of all parameter authorities throughout the entire invocation: the historical interpretation of reborrows and this property are deferred to Spec 3.

Properties of transfer between threads and shareability do not follow from this sequential model alone. They depend on external resources, contained authorities, anchors, confinement restrictions, and the concurrency model of Spec 2.

def LocalShape.toShape (ls : LocalShape) : List (Option Nat × Option Nat × Nat) :=
  ls.map fun e => (e.1, none, e.2)

/-- Owner of element `i` of a shape (§47, §72, §71): its owning element if any, `hd`
otherwise. -/
def shapeOwner (ls : List (Option Nat × Option Nat × Nat)) (hd : Holder) (i : Nat) : Holder :=
  match (ls[i]?).bind (·.2.1) with
  | some o => .place o
  | none => hd

/-- Places `P` followed by the elements of a shape (§47, §71, §72): (parent, owning element,
kind), owned by their owning element or by `hd`. -/
def shapeP (P : List Place) (hd : Holder) (ls : List (Option Nat × Option Nat × Nat)) :
    List Place :=
  P ++ (List.range ls.length).map fun i =>
    ⟨(ls[i]?).bind (·.1), shapeOwner ls hd i, ((ls[i]?).map (·.2.2)).getD 0⟩

/-- Well-formed shape at offset `n` (§72.2, §71.1; for statics, the hypothesis recorded for
§47): the parent and the owning element of an element are earlier elements, and a part has the
owning element of its parent. -/
def ShapeOK (n : Nat) (ls : List (Option Nat × Option Nat × Nat)) : Prop :=
  ∀ i ∈ List.range ls.length,
    OptP ((ls[i]?).bind (·.1)) (fun r => n ≤ r ∧ r < n + i ∧
      (ls[i]?).bind (·.2.1) = (ls[r - n]?).bind (·.2.1)) True ∧
    OptP ((ls[i]?).bind (·.2.1)) (fun o => n ≤ o ∧ o < n + i) True

/-- Decidability of `ShapeOK` (§72.2, §71.1). -/
instance (n : Nat) (ls : List (Option Nat × Option Nat × Nat)) : Decidable (ShapeOK n ls) := by
  unfold ShapeOK; infer_instance

/-- Indices of the root elements (no parent) of a shape (§40 root places; §47, §71, §72). -/
def rootIdx (ls : List (Option Nat × Option Nat × Nat)) : List Nat :=
  (List.range ls.length).filter fun i => ((ls[i]?).bind (·.1)).isNone

/-! ## Kernel steps (§57, §58) -/

/-- One `ok` transition of a kernel operation O1–O16 (§60–§75; §57 reachability). -/
inductive KStep (k : K) : S3 → S3 → Prop where
  | derive {s s' : S3} {src : Nat} {region : List Nat} {m : Mode} :
      DeriveStep src region m s (.ok s') → KStep k s s'
  | split {s s' : S3} {src : Nat} {rs : List (List Nat)} :
      SplitStep k src rs s (.ok s') → KStep k s s'
  | release {s s' : S3} {a : Nat} : ReleaseStep a s (.ok s') → KStep k s s'
  | transfer {s s' : S3} {src dst : Nat} : TransferStep k src dst s (.ok s') → KStep k s s'
  | depend {s s' : S3} {q x : Nat} : DependStep q x s (.ok s') → KStep k s s'
  | enter {s s' : S3} {ps : List Nat} {ls : LocalShape} :
      EnterStep ps ls s (.ok s') → KStep k s s'
  | exit {s s' : S3} : ExitStep k s (.ok s') → KStep k s s'
  | read {s s' : S3} {a : Nat} {ls : List Nat} : Read3Step a ls s (.ok s') → KStep k s s'
  | write {s s' : S3} {a : Nat} {ls : List Nat} : Write3Step a ls s (.ok s') → KStep k s s'
  | writeShared {s s' : S3} {a : Nat} {ls : List Nat} :
      WriteSharedStep k a ls s (.ok s') → KStep k s s'
  | pin {s s' : S3} {p : Nat} : PinStep p s (.ok s') → KStep k s s'
  | unpin {s s' : S3} {p : Nat} : UnpinStep k p s (.ok s') → KStep k s s'
  | endUse {s s' : S3} {p : Nat} : EndUseStep k p s (.ok s') → KStep k s s'
  | free {s s' : S3} {p auth : Nat} : FreeStep k p auth s (.ok s') → KStep k s s'
  | alloc {s s' : S3} {pr ow : Nat} {ls : LocalShape} :
      AllocStep k pr ow ls s (.ok s') → KStep k s s'
  | store {s s' : S3} {a p : Nat} : StoreStep a p s (.ok s') → KStep k s s'

/-! ## Dependencies and anchors (§44) -/

/-- Anchors of the value at `q`, inherited from its parts (§44: dependencies of contained values
are accounted for transitively). -/
def depsOf (s : S3) (q : Nat) : List Nat :=
  ((List.range s.P.length).filter fun r => decide (partOf s.P r q)).flatMap s.D

/-- The anchors of every place containing leaf `p` are valid, that is, active (§44; §66.3,
§67.3, §68.3). -/
def DepsValid (s : S3) (p : Nat) : Prop :=
  ∀ q ∈ List.range s.P.length, partOf s.P p q → ∀ x ∈ s.D q, s.Active x

/-- Decidability of `DepsValid` (§44). -/
instance (s : S3) (p : Nat) : Decidable (DepsValid s p) :=
  inferInstanceAs (Decidable (∀ _ ∈ _, _))

/-- The frame of the effective anchor of `x` (the frame of its holder) exists and is `fd` or an
ancestor of `fd` (§44). -/
def EffAnchorOK (s : S3) (x : Nat) (fd : Option Nat) : Prop :=
  OptP (s.A[s.effAnchor x]?) (fun z => OptP (s.hframe z.holder)
    (fun g => OptP fd (fun f => ancestor s.F g f) False) False) False

/-- Decidability of `EffAnchorOK` (§44). -/
instance (s : S3) (x : Nat) (fd : Option Nat) : Decidable (EffAnchorOK s x fd) := by
  unfold EffAnchorOK; infer_instance

/-- `AnchorOrder` (§44, §54): for every anchor `x ∈ D(q)` of a usable place `q`, the frame of the
effective anchor of `x` is the frame of `q` or an ancestor. -/
def AnchorOrder (s : S3) : Prop := ∀ q, s.Usable q → ∀ x ∈ s.D q, EffAnchorOK s x (s.pframe q)

/-- `AnchorOrder` read on the places of `P` (decision procedure for §44). -/
theorem anchorOrder_iff {s : S3} : AnchorOrder s ↔
    ∀ q ∈ List.range s.P.length, s.Usable q → ∀ x ∈ s.D q, EffAnchorOK s x (s.pframe q) :=
  ⟨fun h q _ hq => h q hq, fun h q hq => h q (List.mem_range.2 hq.lt) hq⟩

/-- Decidability of `AnchorOrder` (§44). -/
instance (s : S3) : Decidable (AnchorOrder s) := decidable_of_iff _ anchorOrder_iff.symm

/-- `AnchorOrderHeld` (§44, §54): the rule of `AnchorOrder` for every active authority held by a
usable place `q`. -/
def AnchorOrderHeld (s : S3) : Prop :=
  ∀ q, s.Usable q → ∀ (x : Nat) (y : Authority), s.A[x]? = some y → y.active = true →
    y.holder = .place q → EffAnchorOK s x (s.pframe q)

/-- `AnchorOrderHeld` read on the places of `P` and the authorities of `A` (decision procedure for
§44). -/
theorem anchorOrderHeld_iff {s : S3} : AnchorOrderHeld s ↔
    ∀ q ∈ List.range s.P.length, s.Usable q → ∀ x ∈ List.range s.A.length,
      OptP (s.A[x]?) (fun y => y.active = true → y.holder = .place q →
        EffAnchorOK s x (s.pframe q)) True := by
  constructor
  · intro h q _ hq x _
    unfold OptP; split
    · rename_i y hy; exact h q hq x y hy
    · trivial
  · intro h q hq x y hy ya hh
    have := h q (List.mem_range.2 hq.lt) hq x (List.mem_range.2 (lt_of_getElem? hy))
    simp only [OptP, hy] at this; exact this ya hh

/-- Decidability of `AnchorOrderHeld` (§44). -/
instance (s : S3) : Decidable (AnchorOrderHeld s) := decidable_of_iff _ anchorOrderHeld_iff.symm

- kstep_iff and reachable_iff give an exact Step/Reachable correspondence.
